intended_object: The restriction e|_H of an automorphism e of a group object G to a characteristic subgroup object i : H ↪ G. It is the unique automorphism of H with e|_H ≫ i = i ≫ e. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The class `Characteristic` asserts that for every automorphism e of `Grp.mk G` there is an automorphism eH of `Grp.mk H` with eH ≫ i = i ≫ e. This is the categorical version of the requirement that every automorphism maps H onto H. Asking for an iso is right: classically φ(H) ⊆ H for all automorphisms φ, and applying this to φ⁻¹ gives equality. `liftIso` picks such an eH with `Exists.choose`. Since i is mono, the restriction is unique; `liftIso_unique` proves this right below the definition. So the choice is canonical and the definition is exactly the restricted automorphism. The setting, group objects in an arbitrary cartesian monoidal category, is already general. It covers ordinary groups and group schemes. I know of no Mathlib definition of this restriction for group objects; Mathlib has characteristic subgroups only for ordinary groups (`Subgroup.Characteristic`).
